[[Eddie Keher]] | team2 = Galway | captain2 = [[Joe McDonagh]] | manager2 = [[Babs Keating|Michael "Babs" Keating]] | totalgoals = 43 (4.3 per game) | totalpoints = 271 (27.1 per game) | topscorer = [[Éamonn Cregan]] (2–17) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1978|1978]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1980|1980]] }} The '''1979 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 93rd staging of the All-Ireland [[hurling]] championship since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The championship began on 27 May 1979 and ended on 2 September 1978. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] entered the championship as [[1978 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the All-Ireland semi-final.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2013/0425/385551-waiting-in-the-long-grass/|title=Waiting in the Long Grass|publisher=RTÉ Sport website|date=26 April 2013|access-date=30 October 2013|first=Rory|last=O'Neill}} [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after defeating Galway by 2–12 to 1–8 in the [[1979 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]]. ==Teams== A total of eleven teams contested the championship, one of the fewest participants in years. Only four team contested the Leinster series of games. [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]] and [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] withdrew from the provincial campaign, however, Laois did qualify for the All-Ireland series by winning the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]]. They did this at [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]'s expense. referee = G Ryan (Tipperary) }} {{main|1979 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final}} ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * [[Cork GAA|Cork]] capture a record-equalling fifth successive Munster title following a victory over [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]. It is the second time that Cork have achieved the five-in-a-row, the first since 1905. * In the All-Ireland semi-final, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] defeat Cork for only the second time in the history of the championship. It is Cork's first defeat since the All-Ireland semi-final of 1975 when the same opposition recorded their first win over 'the Rebels'. ==Top scorers== ===Season=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! Rank !
